name: SHUAA Capital
founded: 1979 (as Arabian General Investment Corporation, by Emiri Decree No. 6 of 25 Apr 1979); merged with Abu Dhabi Financial Group (ADFG) in 2019 via a reverse takeover in which ADFG was the accounting acquirer
ownership_summary: DFM-listed. At 31 Dec 2025, holders above 5% were YAS Global FZE (18.894%) and SICO B.S.C. (7.317%), out of 3,659.0m shares and 10,004 shareholders; 69.26% of shares were held by UAE investors. Share capital rose from AED 2,535.7m to AED 3,659.0m in Q1 2025 when mandatory convertible bonds (MCBs) were converted at AED 0.32 per share.
government_link: Indirect board links only: the Chairman is Director General of the Abu Dhabi Investment Office and the Vice Chair is an ADQ executive (official board page, checked 2026-10-12). Neither ADQ nor the Abu Dhabi government appears among holders above 5% at 31 Dec 2025. Who owns YAS Global FZE was not established.
group_structure: SHUAA Capital PSC (DFM) is the legal parent; ADFG is the accounting acquirer from the 2019 reverse takeover. Material subsidiaries at 31 Dec 2025 include ADCM Ltd (Cayman, investment management), Northacre Limited (UK real-estate development management, 83.9%) and Northacre Capital, Integrated Capital PJSC (UAE, 96%), Amwal International Investment Company KSCP (Kuwait, 87.2%), SHUAA Capital Saudi Arabia CJSC (100%), Qannas Investments (80.8%) and Spadille (85%). Gulf Finance Corporation (UAE/KSA) and ADCORP are under liquidation. Material associate: Eshraq Investments PJSC (21.37%), the subject of the auditor's qualification. SHUAA GMC operates under the ADGM framework (per management page). Operating segments: Asset Management, Investment Banking, Corporate.

business_lines: Asset Management: public markets (Middle East equity and fixed-income funds), private markets (growth capital, direct investments), real estate (development management via Northacre, fund management), debt/private credit (Shariah-compliant funds and discretionary mandates). Investment Banking: corporate finance advisory, underwriting, securities services, OTC fixed income sales and trading, credit sales and agency securities lending, and an equity trading business launched in 2026. Corporate: principal investments and legacy assets being wound down.

capabilities.wealth_summary: SHUAA is a DFM-listed Dubai asset manager and investment bank serving institutions and HNW clients, now much smaller after a 2024–2025 balance-sheet restructuring. In Q1 2025 it converted mandatory convertible bonds into 1.12bn new shares at AED 0.32 and settled other noteholders at 20% of principal. A bank term loan (AED 221m) is still being restructured under waivers extended to 31 Aug 2026. Revenue (AED 82m in FY2025) is mainly management fees from public-markets funds, private markets, real estate (Northacre) and Shariah-compliant private-debt funds and discretionary mandates. Investment banking added OTC fixed-income trading, credit sales, agency securities lending and a new equity trading business in 2026. A Head of Product and Structuring joined in 2026. The FY2025 deck shows AUM of 4,895m (labelled AED m; currency to confirm). No retail app, robo or digital investing platform was found; clients use a portal (shuaaconnect.com).

AUM 4,895m per FY2025 deck (currency to confirm); fiduciary clients' funds AED 5.9bn at a CBUAE-licensed subsidiary.

brokerage.detail: Institutional: OTC fixed income/currencies/commodities sales and trading, securities services, agency securities lending, and an equity trading business launched in 2026 (Head of Equity Trading). Trading and custody revenue AED 8.5m in H1 2026. No retail brokerage app found.

digital_investing.detail: Only a client portal (shuaaconnect.com/investrack) linked from the website; no retail investing app.

advisory.detail: Corporate finance advisory (advisory fees AED 17.2m FY2025); SCA licence covers financial consulting and analysis; non-discretionary advice not described.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary mandates in the debt strategy; investment portfolios managed in Asset Management segment.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds only; no third-party fund distribution shelf found.

structured_products.detail: Investment Banking segment description includes structured products; a Head of Product and Structuring joined in 2026.

private_markets.detail: Private markets (growth capital, bolt-on acquisitions), real estate funds and private debt; May 2026 advisory partnership with Key Capital (Key Fund I LP, USD 50m target, ADGM, VC secondaries).

islamic_wealth.detail: Private-debt strategies delivered through Shariah-compliant funds and discretionary mandates.

partners.what: SHUAA provides capital formation, strategic relationships and capital markets execution for Key Fund I LP (USD 50m target, ADGM LP)
MoU targeting consolidation of Saudi Arabia's fuel retail sector

initiatives.what: Completed balance-sheet restructuring: AED 274.4m MCBs converted at AED 0.32/share (857.5m shares), AED 85m new MCBs (265.6m shares), remaining noteholders settled at 20% of principal; equity rose from AED 41m to AED 554m by end-2025
Launched equity trading business; hired Head of Product and Structuring
Strategic partnership with Key Capital on MENA venture capital secondaries
Q2 2026 results: return to quarterly profit (AED 9.1m); still negotiating restructuring/refinancing of its bank facility (waiver to 31 Aug 2026)

opportunities: Rebuilding its revenue base after restructuring and adding product and structuring capability (new Head of Product and Structuring, 2026) to an institutional/HNW franchise with no digital client platform beyond a portal (S2, S3, S7).
Has private-markets, real-estate and Shariah private-debt product that could be packaged for wealth distribution (S4, S9).
barriers: Financial fragility: going-concern note with AED 307m borrowings due within 12 months, bank waiver to 31 Aug 2026, accumulated losses AED 946m; qualified review conclusion over Eshraq (S5).
Small, cost-constrained operation (cost-to-income 99% in FY2025; revenue AED 82m) (S7).
